hooks.text: A suicide probe hit comet dust at 150,000 mph.
It plunged into a comet at 150,000 miles per hour.
A tiny spacecraft took a direct, high-speed comet hit.

title: Surviving a Comet Blast at 150,000 MPH
description: How Europe's Giotto probe survived a punishing swarm of comet dust to snap the first close-up images of Halley's nucleus.

beats.text: A suicide probe hit comet dust at 150,000 mph.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of Giotto spacecraft encountering Halley's Comet, 1986

beats.text: Engineers protected it with a shield of aluminum and Kevlar.
beats.visual: Whipple shield spacecraft diagram showing aluminum and Kevlar layers

beats.text: The craft passed within 596 kilometers of the icy nucleus.
beats.visual: Halley Multicolour Camera nucleus photograph by Giotto, 1986

beats.text: Right before, a dust particle knocked it spinning off axis.
beats.visual: Artist's illustration of Giotto spinning after dust impact, 1986

beats.text: The resilient probe somehow re-stabilized itself within 32 minutes.
beats.visual: Giotto spacecraft model on display at European Space Research and Technology Centre

beats.text: It captured the first close-up images of a peanut-shaped nucleus.
beats.visual: Comet Halley nucleus imaged by Giotto Multicolour Camera, 1986

beats.text: That is how a suicide probe hit comet dust at 150,000 mph.
beats.visual: Extended mission trajectory graphic for Giotto spacecraft, 1992

better_than_last: Applied the proven narrative arc from ep137 by placing the recovery resolution near the climax and building a tight loop that directly echoes the hook's exact phrasing.
